title: Test comment misquotes the reconstructed JS tail: shows `},” where the shipped literal ends `;,`
evidence: Line 83: `// js === "sanitize_properties:function(p){...return scrub(p);},"` — but server/src/application/form_view.gleam:308 ships `<> "return scrub(p);,"` (the literal content ends `return scrub(p);,` with no `}` before the comma). The joined literals end `...return o;};return scrub(p);,`.
detail: In a file whose stated purpose is byte-fidelity of the shipped snippet, the comment misdescribes the exact tail of the extracted JS. Harmless (the `...` ellipsis makes it illustrative), but it could mislead a future editor into thinking the trailing comma is a standalone separator.
recommended_fix: Change the comment to `// js === "sanitize_properties:function(p){...return scrub(p);,"` (drop the `}`), matching the actual literal at form_view.gleam:308.
